idiom_name: async enrich function / Vapor AsyncMiddleware over a DataSource protocol
implementation_notes: Swift's async/await makes the enricher a throwing async function over a DataSource protocol; on the server, Vapor's AsyncMiddleware (respond(to:chainingTo:) async throws) is the insertion point, so enrichment runs in the responder chain before the handler and awaits the resource without blocking an event-loop thread. A cache in front of the source must be an actor (or lock-guarded) to be safe across concurrent requests, and the enriched value type carries the merged fields while failures travel the typed throws path. The old EventLoopFuture-based Middleware protocol still works but must never be blocked with .wait().
pitfalls: Vapor's Request storage is per-request, but a class-based cache shared across requests races - make it an actor or guard it with a lock.
Awaiting the resource inside middleware adds latency to every route it is attached to; scope it with route groups instead of installing it globally.
The non-async Middleware protocol returns EventLoopFuture and must not be blocked with .wait(), which deadlocks the event loop.
